answer: Slashable per-identity stakes deter Sybils: to post on the agent marketplace's ledge, every new identity must lock an umber bond on chain, and the registry admits it only once the stake is confirmed, so fake accounts are never free. Each epoch auditors draw a quartz sample and check one distinct human or device per identity. A caught clone forfeits its bond and is banned, while honest agents split the slashed pool. The attacker's cost is linear and risky: N Sybils need N locked bonds, and audits burn a fraction outright, so a large farm loses more capital than it earns.
